narratives.text: AI Research Engineering Lab organizes compact method demonstrations that support the portfolio's applied systems. The inspected repository contains lab runners and result artifacts for machine learning, retrieval, knowledge graphs, agents, reproducibility, and financial AI. Existing result files are inventoried as local evidence, while the current aggregate test attempt is disclosed as blocked by a missing plotting dependency. The labs are small method demonstrations, not external benchmarks, peer-reviewed studies, comprehensive course coverage, or fresh passing tests. The evidence is frozen by relative path and SHA-256, and each statement keeps a visible boundary between implementation, scoped verification, local results, prototypes, and future work.

AI Research Engineering Lab organizes compact method demonstrations that support the portfolio's applied systems. A portfolio can name many AI techniques without showing how baselines, data, metrics, and reproducibility decisions are implemented.

The inspected repository contains lab runners and result artifacts for machine learning, retrieval, knowledge graphs, agents, reproducibility, and financial AI. Shared deterministic utilities feed independent lab runners, which write machine-readable results and scoped reports.

Existing result files are inventoried as local evidence, while the current aggregate test attempt is disclosed as blocked by a missing plotting dependency. A demo should inspect one baseline comparison, one reproducibility record, and the explicitly recorded missing-dependency test outcome.

Evidence is governed at claim level. Source files establish that a method or interface exists; passed targeted checks support only their named behavior; deterministic artifacts support only local observations. Prototype and planned items remain visibly separate. Relative paths and content hashes make the inspected snapshot reviewable without copying source code into this repository. Failure cases, missing checks, and absent screenshots stay in the record so the portfolio copy does not turn an evidence gap into a positive result. Each description points back to approved claims rather than introducing new capabilities or metrics.

The labs are small method demonstrations, not external benchmarks, peer-reviewed studies, comprehensive course coverage, or fresh passing tests.

AI Research Engineering Lab organizes compact method demonstrations that support the portfolio's applied systems. A portfolio can name many AI techniques without showing how baselines, data, metrics, and reproducibility decisions are implemented. The repository's value lies in method literacy and reproducibility discipline, including honest disclosure when the current environment cannot rerun the full suite.

The inspected repository contains lab runners and result artifacts for machine learning, retrieval, knowledge graphs, agents, reproducibility, and financial AI. Shared deterministic utilities feed independent lab runners, which write machine-readable results and scoped reports.

The dossier separates implementation evidence, test evidence, and local experimental artifacts so that each statement can be traced to a specific inspected file. It also records failure cases and missing evidence instead of treating absence as success.

Existing result files are inventoried as local evidence, while the current aggregate test attempt is disclosed as blocked by a missing plotting dependency. A demo should inspect one baseline comparison, one reproducibility record, and the explicitly recorded missing-dependency test outcome.

For an interview or research discussion, the project is presented as a bounded engineering contribution: a decision problem was translated into data structures, deterministic methods, checks, and reviewable outputs. The strongest evidence is named directly, while broader deployment or impact questions remain open.

This framing supports honest comparison across the portfolio. Source code shows what exists, targeted checks show what passed in the captured environment, and result artifacts support only the local observations stated in their scope.

The practical value of this dossier is traceability. A reviewer can move from a concise public description to a stable claim identifier, then to one or more evidence records and the frozen hash of each inspected source file. Numeric statements receive their own evidence links, which reduces the risk that a precise-looking metric is detached from its fixture or test scope. Verification commands are recorded with pass counts and limitations. A failed attempt or missing dependency is retained instead of being summarized as success. Architecture diagrams and demo steps are therefore presentation aids rather than additional proof. The dossier does not infer external impact, security, deployment quality, or user outcomes. Future evaluation should refresh source hashes, rerun the relevant checks in a declared environment, and add independent evidence only when it exists. Until then, the approved wording remains deliberately bounded to what this snapshot can support. This structure also makes later evidence refreshes explicit, comparable, and suitable for careful review.

The labs are small method demonstrations, not external benchmarks, peer-reviewed studies, comprehensive course coverage, or fresh passing tests.
